A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVOO research. All pages, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable. Relocated material can be matched, and v2's omission of Appendix B.2-B.8 is distinguishable from extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original quality and latency benchmarks across seven video-generation models, component ablations, clustering analyses, and supplementary sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains the original seven-model benchmarks in Tables 1-2, component ablations, and attention sparsity and clustering analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same offline sparsity profiling, Gaussian-quantile schedule, bidirectional Q-K co-clustering, block selection, and clustering reuse procedures. Removing implementation disclosures does not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Penguin/VBench prompts for text-to-video and VBench++ image-prompt pairs for image-to-video across the same seven Wan and HunyuanVideo models. The omitted supplementary experiments and examples concern this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain dense attention, SpargeAttention, SVG/SVG1, SVG2, and Radial. Section 5.6 retains the SVG2 k-means comparison. Deleting the supplementary VBench metric table does not change the comparator set within the retained benchmarks.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation loses three VBench metrics: temporal flickering, motion smoothness, and overall consistency. It also loses protocols sweeping reuse intervals up to 30 steps, query blocks from 64 to 512, key blocks from 256 to 2048, and warm-up from 0% to 25%. Retained Section 5.1 settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the studies of how reuse frequency, query/key block counts, and dense-attention warm-up affect quality and latency (B.3-B.5, Table 4, Figures 12-13), plus additional qualitative examples in B.6/Figure 14. The main component ablation and clustering stability/recall analyses remain.

E5.justification: Empirical uncertainty reporting is unchanged: neither version supplies evaluation seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The five-input sparsity plots and Gaussian fitting procedure are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 are numerically identical, including SVOO's 29.986 dB PSNR, 216-second latency, and 1.93x speedup on Wan2.1-1.3B-T2V. V2 removes Table 3's additional quality scores, Table 4's block-count results, the reuse and warm-up curves, and additional generated-video examples. These are lost results, not revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumption 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and Appendix A derivations and proof are unchanged. Correcting the explanatory reference from Equation (8) to Equation (4) changes navigation, not mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same input-stability claim, two-stage contribution, and superior quality-speed trade-off claim across seven models. The new title foregrounds input stability already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Deleting B.3-B.7 removes substantive interpretations about safe clustering reuse, diminishing returns from increasing block counts, benefits of longer warm-up, and negligible offline calibration overhead. It also removes B.5's training and learning-rate explanation of warm-up. The central input-stability and Q-K coupling interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link in the abstract but removes the disclosure of 10 GPT-5-generated calibration inputs and B.8's top-50%-attention-mass reference and budget description for the retained recall experiment. Hardware, kernels, and default settings remain documented. These are disclosure changes, not evidence of changed execution.

R1.justification: The introduction and bibliography replace the Open-Sora-Plan and Open-Sora references by Lin et al. (2024) and Zheng et al. (2024) with two Gaussian-splatting papers by Wang et al. (2025, 2026). The detailed sparse-attention related work and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, trims introductory prose, corrects an equation cross-reference, and adds acknowledgements and ICML header/footer text, including a template-style running header. The surviving scientific narrative and section sequence are largely verbatim; appendix deletions chiefly remove scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 removes Tables 3-4 and Figures 12-14, redistributes Tables 1-2 across separate pages, relocates the framework diagram and algorithm, and swaps the numbering of the qualitative-example and ablation figures. Figure 1's caption is shortened. Retained visual results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, proof, and main benchmarks remain intact, but v2 substantially reduces evidence for parameter robustness and the quality-speed trade-off by deleting the supplementary metrics and sensitivity studies. Removing calibration and recall-comparison details also weakens reproducibility, while Section 5.6 still points to absent appendix material. The code link, corrected cross-reference, and removal of the inconsistent training-based warm-up explanation provide limited benefits that do not offset these losses.
